text:
support-alex: FYI customer reported function-call failing when streaming — args arrive as a partial JSON chunk and parser errors. stack: /v1/chat/stream -> tool invocation. payload sample attached. :frowning:
eng-ryan: can you drop the minimal repro + which client (node/python/other)?
customer-bob: node 18 fetch streaming. repro steps:
  1) POST /v1/chat/stream with function call schema and streaming: true
  2) client keeps connection open, reading SSE chunks
  3) tool receives truncated args mid-key, parse error on server side
example of captured chunk (from customer):
```
data: {"tool":"charge","args":{"user_id":"u-123","amount":29\n```
next chunk in stream: ````
data: "","currency":"usd"}\n```` (so the JSON split happens mid-string/field)
support-alex: error observed is `JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at` in customer's tool handler. they see this intermittently (~1/20 streams) and on large payloads.
eng-ryan: thanks. can you paste raw http headers (client + our edge/proxy) and whether Transfer-Encoding: chunked or Content-Length is used? also example of TLS termination point.
customer-bob: headers from client -> our-edge:
  Host: api.redwood.example
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  User-Agent: custom-node/1.2
  Keep-Alive: timeout=60
edge logs show proxied to backend with `X-Proxy-Chunk-Size: 4096` and `X-Forwarded-For: ...`
sre-jen: :eyes: our nginx default chunked config can split at buffer boundaries; if a chunk boundary falls inside a UTF-8 multibyte char or JSON token you'll see mid-json splits. check `proxy_buffer_size` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size`. also confirm `proxy_request_buffering off` for streaming routes.
eng-ryan: good call. also suspect intermediate LB doing re-chunking. can we rule out client-side flushes? suggest a small harness: use `curl -N` and a tiny node script that intentionally writes a partial JSON then sleeps then writes remainder to reproduce.
proxy-bot: INFO 2938500200 re-chunked stream: client->edge chunks [2048, 1024, 512], edge->backend chunks [1024,512,512,512]. detected split inside JSON string at offset 187.
support-alex: customer attached a raw pcap and the split matches proxy re-chunking. they're blocked in production; asking for hotfix.
eng-ryan: short-term mitigation: update our function-call parser to buffer until a full top-level JSON object is seen, using a small incremental parser (e.g., keep reading until braces match or attempt incremental streaming JSON parser). long-term: make stream framing explicit (SSE event per complete JSON payload) or require a newline-delimited JSON wrapper.
sre-jen: for immediate rollout I can flip `proxy_request_buffering off` + increase `proxy_buffer_size` on canary edge for this route and monitor error rate. will also add a filter to ensure chunk boundaries are only at event boundaries if client sends `X-Event-Length` header.
eng-ryan: I'll prepare a tiny patch: server will accept partial reads but attempt to reassemble using a small stateful buffer keyed by connection id, max buffer 1MB, parse when we detect balanced braces. fallback to current behavior after timeout. PR in progress.
support-alex: customer asked for ETA — can we get a canary in 2h?
sre-jen: canary in 90m, monitoring set for `toolcall_json_parse_errors` and 5xx spikes. will rollback if error increases.
customer-bob: appreciate the quick turnaround. attaching a minimal node repro script:```js
const net = require('net');
const req = `POST /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n`
// socket write partial json then wait
// ...
```
eng-ryan: thanks, will use that to reproduce locally. plan: 1) canary nginx buffer tweak, 2) server reassemble patch, 3) encourage clients to send event-per-json or newline delimiting in docs.
support-alex: noted. I'll message the customer with the mitigation plan and ETA. :thumbsup:
eng-ryan: assigning to @sre-jen and @eng-ryan for rollout; I'll open a support ticket linking this thread and the PR.
sre-jen: monitoring alert live. will report back with metrics in ~1h. :hourglass:
